clauses.reason: The operative command revokes Executive Order 2414 of June 30, 1916 and the order becomes effective at the close of business on December 31, 1953. The revocation is a one-time act, performed when the order was issued, so the clause was spent on signing, January 19, 1954; the filing date, January 20, 1954, is the alternative reading. The order's effective-date sentence dates the revocation of Executive Order 2414 back to the close of business on December 31, 1953; that is the end of the revoked order and falls before this order existed, so it is not the end of this clause. No later order is held that postpones, amends or revokes this order.

inventory_overrides.reason: The dossier's lead clause (characters 3415 to 3962) ends at the words 'December 31,' and a second clause holds only the final year, 1953, of the same effective-date sentence. The operative revocation and its effective-date sentence are one command, so I use one clause covering both.

research_rationale:
EO 10514 (signed 1954-01-19 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-01-20, 10:29 a.m.; 19 FR 369, Federal Register of January 21, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10514.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. The dossier split the order into a lead clause and a stray clause holding only the last year of the effective-date sentence; I replace them with one clause (characters 3415 to 3970 of the registered file), which holds the whole order: under the act of March 12, 1914 (38 Stat. 305) and on the Secretary of the Interior's recommendation, it revokes Executive Order 2414 of June 30, 1916 (hospital-service regulations for the construction and operation of the Government railway in Alaska, now the Alaska Railroad), and the order becomes effective at the close of business on December 31, 1953. First end: the revocation is a one-time act and was performed when the order was issued, so the clause was spent on signing, January 19, 1954; the filing date, January 20, 1954 (10:29 a.m.), is the alternative reading. The effective-date sentence makes the revocation of Executive Order 2414 effective retroactively at the close of business on December 31, 1953. That fixes when Executive Order 2414 is treated as ceasing; it cannot fix when this order's own command was performed, because this order did not exist on that date, so December 31, 1953 is the end of the revoked order and not of this one. The consequence, that Executive Order 2414 no longer applies, is a completed result and not a continuing command. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10514 found only the order's own copies, the earlier orders printed in the same issue and unrelated page numbers; none amends, postpones or revokes it. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts).
